review: 1:1–1:4 the Arabic is 2 Timothy 1:9 (الَّذِي خَلَّصَنَا وَدَعَانَا دَعْوَةً مُقَدَّسَةً … بِحَسَبِ قَصْدِهِ وَنِعْمَتِهِ … لَا بِحَسَبِ أَعْمَالِنَا); the Hebrew keeps the same four elements in the same order, including the 'not by works' turn at the end of the stanza.

2:2 לִפְנֵי־עַד — the Arabic قَبْلَ الدُّهُورِ is 'before the ages'; לִפְנֵי־עַד is the biblical phrase for 'before everlasting' (Ps 55:20; Hab 1:12), so the line does not need the Modern Hebrew נִצְחִיּוּת.

2:4 בְּאִישׁוּתוֹ נִגְלָה — the Arabic بِشَخْصِهِ قَدْ أُظْهِرَتْ is 'in His person it was revealed'; the glossary noun אִישׁוּת ('personhood') is used, but as a predicate of the revealing, not as an abstract doctrine.

3:3–3:4 אֵין לוֹ רֵאשִׁית … וְלֹא חֵקֶר — the Arabic لَيْسَ لَهَا بَدْءٌ وَلَا / حَدٌّ يُرَى وَلَا قَرَار is 'no beginning, no visible bound, no limit'; the Hebrew keeps all three negations with biblical nouns (רֵאשִׁית, קֵץ, חֵקֶר) rather than the Arabic's two.

5:4 בְּיֵשׁוּעַ הֶעָשִׁיר — the Arabic فِي الرَّبِّ يَسُوعَ الْغَنِيِّ keeps 'the rich' from 2 Cor 8:9; the Hebrew keeps הֶעָשִׁיר as an attribute so the stanza closes on the same contrast with which hymn 159 opens.
